title: Digital Billboard Pricing - Flexible, Pay-As-You-Go Ads | Blip

facts.fact: Blip digital billboard advertising starts at $0.01 per display.
Blip digital billboard advertising starts at $0.01 per 8-second play, with no monthly minimum and no contract.
facts.quote: Blip digital billboard advertising starts at $0.01 per 8-second play. There's no monthly minimum and no contract

facts.fact: Blip's platform shows real-time pricing for all 3,500+ digital billboards (vendor's own claim).
facts.quote: Blip's platform shows real-time pricing for all 3,500+ digital billboards before you commit a dollar.

facts.fact: According to Blip's FAQ, a traditional digital billboard 4-week lease averages $3,953 per month nationally (figure cited by vendor, source not given on page).
facts.quote: traditional billboard pricing, which averages $3,953 per month and ranges from $250 to $100,000+ depending on market

facts.fact: Per Blip's FAQ, traditional billboard pricing ranges from $250 in rural markets to $100,000+ in premium urban locations.
facts.quote: ranges from $250 in rural markets to $100,000+ in premium urban locations

facts.fact: Blip states there is no required minimum budget and no contract for billboard advertising; advertisers can start with a few dollars per day.
facts.quote: There's no required minimum and no contract. You can start with just a few dollars per day to test a single market

facts.fact: Blip states it charges no setup fees, platform fees, agency fees, or monthly retainers.
facts.quote: No. Blip doesn't charge setup fees, platform fees, agency fees, or monthly retainers.

facts.fact: Blip digital billboards are sold in 8-second displays; a 30-second ad is not sold as one block on Blip.
facts.quote: Blip uses digital billboard advertising pricing based on 8-second displays.

facts.fact: Blip's FAQ says billboard cost is mainly affected by location, traffic volume, time of day, and advertiser demand.
facts.quote: Billboard advertising cost is mainly affected by location, traffic volume, time of day, and advertiser demand.

facts.fact: The SafeSiblings.org case study ran short hourly bursts across 1,000 billboards in hundreds of cities (vendor-reported customer example).
facts.quote: By running short, hourly bursts across 1,000 billboards in hundreds of cities
